questions.question: Explain why galvanising is used on steel gate hinges but not on stainless steel hinges.
questions.correctAnswer: Steel contains iron which rusts. Galvanising coats with zinc - zinc corrodes sacrificially, protecting exposed iron even if scratched. Stainless steel has 10.5%+ chromium forming a self-healing oxide layer - does not rust, so galvanising is unnecessary.

questions.question: Compare varnish and oil as finishes for an oak dining table, justifying your recommendation for a family home.
questions.correctAnswer: Varnish: hard clear film - excellent waterproof protection, resists scratches and heat, easy to wipe clean. Oil: penetrates wood, warm natural look, easy to repair, water-resistant but not waterproof, needs regular reapplication. For a busy family home: varnish for superior protection against spills and scratches.

questions.question: A polymer product needs the company logo applied. Compare pad printing and screen printing.
questions.correctAnswer: Pad printing: transfers ink via silicone pad - excellent for curved/irregular surfaces, small to medium logos, fine detail. Screen printing: ink through mesh stencil - best for flat surfaces, large areas, bold colours. For curved polymer casing: pad printing. For flat panel: screen printing.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response A manufacturer produces aluminium outdoor furniture. Evaluate THREE appropriate finishing techniques and recommend the most suitable for a coastal environment. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: identify coastal challenges (salt spray, UV, moisture); evaluate anodising (excellent corrosion resistance, UV stable, oxide layer is integral to aluminium - cannot chip, self-healing); powder coating (good but can chip on edges); painting (least durable - salt penetrates cracks, paint peels). Recommendation: anodising is most suitable for coastal environments.
